publication: Pankratz, L. B. (1982), Thermodynamic Properties of Elements and Oxides, U.S. Bureau of Mines Bulletin 672.

P672-T80.source_note: Table 80, printed p. 80; the 49.500 kcal/mol 298 K anchor is the elemental formation-table value. Thermal data are transcribed from the published row.

P672-T81.source_note: Table 81, printed p. 81; the 52.600 kcal/mol 298 K anchor is the elemental formation-table value. High-temperature nodes are transcribed from the published row.

P672-T82.source_note: Table 82, printed p. 82; the -137.160 kcal/mol 298 K anchor is the elemental formation-table value. The printed liquid branch begins at the 1098 K fusion marker.

P672-T102.source_note: Table 102, printed p. 102; the -61.700 kcal/mol 298 K anchor is from the elemental formation table and CODATA. Other thermal data from Mills.

P672-Se-g.source_note: Pankratz Bulletin 672 selenium gas table, printed p. 367; 56.250 kcal/mol is derived from the printed 0.5 Se2(g)=Se(g) reaction value, 39.600 kcal/mol, plus half the printed Se2(g) elemental formation value, 33.300 kcal/mol. It is not a printed formation-table cell. Thermal data from Mills (158).

P672-Se2-g.source_note: Pankratz Bulletin 672 selenium gas table, printed pp. 368-369; the 33.300 kcal/mol 298 K anchor is the elemental formation-table value. Data from Mills (158). Printed entropy nodes at 1400 K and 1800 K match the scan, and the printed Cp equation agrees within rounding.

P672-Te-g.source_note: Table 415, printed p. 415; 50.600 kcal/mol is derived from the printed 0.5 Te2(g)=Te(g) reaction value, 31.435 kcal/mol, plus half the printed Te2(g) elemental formation value, 38.330 kcal/mol. It is not a printed formation-table cell. Data from Mills (158).

P672-Te2-g.source_note: Table 416, printed p. 416; 38.330 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table anchor. Source prints 100 K Cp, entropy, and enthalpy nodes to 2000 K; data from Mills (158).

P672-TeO2-g.source_note: Tellurium Dioxide gas table, printed pp. 420-421; -15.100 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table anchor on p. 420. Thermal data from Spoliti (210); formation enthalpy at 298 K from Muenow (164).

P672-SeO2-g.table: Selenium Dioxide gas table, printed pp. 380-381
P672-SeO2-g.equation_node_note: At the printed 958 K boiling node, the table gives Cp=13.251 cal/(mol K), S=76.781 cal/(mol K), and H-H298=8.123 kcal/mol. The published equations give Cp=13.160152, S=76.754946, and H-H298=8.086592, respectively. The runtime high interval is fitted to the printed 1000-1500 K nodes; the printed 958 K row is retained as source data.
P672-SeO2-g.source_note: Elemental formation enthalpy is from the formation table on printed p. 380; gas data from Behrens et al. (12), reaction table on printed p. 381. Printed 1000-1500 K Cp, S, and H-H298 nodes are source data. At the printed 958 K boiling node, Cp/H/S disagree with the published heat-capacity and enthalpy equations by 0.090848 cal/(mol K), 0.036408 kcal/mol, and 0.026054 cal/(mol K); the printed node is retained.

P672-SeO-g.table: Selenium Oxide gas table, printed pp. 376-377
P672-SeO-g.source_note: The elemental formation table on printed p. 376 gives ΔfH°298 = 12.750 kcal/mol; the reaction table on printed p. 377 gives -3.900 kcal/mol for 0.5 Se2(g)+0.5 O2(g)=SeO(g). Cp, S, and H-H298 nodes and thermal data are from Gordon (81).

P672-SeO2-c.source_note: Table 378, printed p. 378; -53.860 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table anchor. The source labels the 413-602 K region estimated and marks 602 K as the SeO2 sublimation point; source equations extend through 602 K.

P672-TeO2-l.table: Tellurium Dioxide condensed-phase formation table, printed p. 418
P672-TeO2-l.source_note: The elemental-formation table on printed p. 418 gives the -77.100 kcal/mol 298 K anchor; the separate reaction table on p. 419 gives -96.265 kcal/mol for 0.5 Te2(g)+O2(g)=TeO2(l). Source marks the 1006 K melting point and 6.760 kcal/mol fusion enthalpy; liquid Cp is 27.600 cal/(mol K). Formation anchor and entropy from Wagman (236); high-temperature liquid data based on Prescher (186) and Mezaki (154).

P672-As-g.source_note: As(g), printed p. 49; 72.120 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table anchor, while the high-temperature table relates gas thermochemistry to the 1/4 As4(g) reference. Thermal data from Hultgren (99).

P672-As2-g.source_note: As2(g), printed p. 50; 52.820 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table anchor. Thermal data from Hultgren (99); source reaction is 2As[cr, 1/4As4(g)] = As2(g).

P672-As4-g.source_note: As4(g), printed p. 52, ideal tetratomic row; 36.640 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table anchor. The ideal triatomic label belongs to As3(g) on p. 51. Thermal data from Hultgren (99).

P672-As4O6-g.source_note: Table 56, printed p. 56; -285.910 kcal/mol is the 298 K elemental formation-table anchor. Above 876 K, the printed enthalpy-of-formation column switches to the 1/4 As4(g) reference; stored 298 K formation remains on the crystal reference. Data from Behrens and Rosenblatt (13).

P672-As2O3-c.source_note: Table 53, printed p. 53; -157.020 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table anchor. Above 360 K data are estimated; low-temperature heat capacity and S298 from Chang (29), formation enthalpy from Wagman (236).

P672-Ag-g.source_note: Table 33, printed p. 33; 68.090 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table 298.15 K cell. Thermal nodes are transcribed through 2000 K. Data from Hilsenrath (98).

P672-Ag2O-c.source_note: Table 34, printed p. 34; -7.420 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table 298.15 K cell. The source marks decomposition near 500 K and supplies no liquid function; 500 K is only the hypothetical construction anchor, not a measured melting point.

P672-Sb-g.source_note: Antimony gas formation table, printed p. 352, supplies printed nodes through 1860 K and the elemental formation-table anchor 62.700 kcal/mol. On p. 353, the 0.5 Sb2(g)=Sb(g) reaction equations extend to 2000 K. At 1900/2000 K derive Sb(g) thermal nodes from those reaction equations and the printed p. 354 Sb2(g) nodes: H_inc(Sb)=0.5 H_inc(Sb2)+ΔrH(T)-ΔrH(298), S(Sb)=0.5 S(Sb2)+[ΔrH(T)-ΔrG(T)]·1000/T, Cp(Sb)=0.5 Cp(Sb2)+dΔrH/dT. Enthalpy is kcal/mol, entropy and Cp are cal/(mol K). The result reproduces the 1860 K Sb(g) table cells within their printed rounding; source nodes extend through 2000 K.

P672-Sb2-g.source_note: Antimony gas table, printed pp. 354-355; 56.300 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table 298.15 K cell. Printed continuation nodes through 2000 K. Data from Hultgren (99).

P672-Sb4-g.source_note: Sb4(g) formation table, printed p. 356; 49.000 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table 298.15 K cell. Reaction table 2Sb2(g)=Sb4(g), printed p. 357, independently reports ΔrH298=-63.600 kcal/mol = 49.000-2(56.300), and closure cells through 2000 K. Data from Hultgren (99).

P672-Sb4O6-g.source_note: Tetrantimony hexoxide gas table, printed p. 361; -290.520 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table 298.15 K cell. The formation reference changes above the Sb melt but the stored anchor remains elemental. Thermal nodes end at 1000 K. Data from Behrens (13).

P672-Sb2O3-c.source_note: Orthorhombic Sb2O3 table, printed p. 358; -169.400 kcal/mol and S298=29.400 cal/(mol K) are the elemental formation and entropy cells. The 928 K marker states fusion enthalpy is insufficiently known, and no liquid function is tabulated. The page notes an 879 K cubic-to-orthorhombic transition, orthorhombic metastability below 879 K, and insufficient data to tabulate the cubic form. High-temperature thermal data are estimated.

P672-Th-g.source_note: Printed p. 423, Th(g) elemental formation table, formation reference Th(c,l); 142.730 kcal/mol is the 298.15 K elemental formation anchor. Thermal nodes are transcribed through 2500 K. Data from Oetting (167).

P672-ThO-g.source_note: Printed p. 424, ThO(g) elemental formation table from Th(c,l)+0.5O2(g); -6.077 kcal/mol is the 298.15 K elemental formation anchor. Thermal nodes are transcribed through 2500 K. Data from Wagman (240).

P672-ThO2-c.source_note: Printed p. 425, ThO2(cr) elemental formation table from Th(c,l)+O2(g); -293.120 kcal/mol is the 298.15 K anchor. Crystal nodes extend through 2500 K; no liquid formation branch is printed. Data from Wagman (240).

P672-ThO2-g.source_note: Printed p. 426, ThO2(g) elemental formation table from Th(c,l)+O2(g); -118.670 kcal/mol is the 298.15 K anchor. Thermal nodes are transcribed through 2500 K. Data from Wagman (240).

P672-Y-g.source_note: Y(g) formation table, printed p. 474; 100.700 kcal/mol is the elemental 298.15 K formation cell. Thermal data follow the source's 298.15-2500 K function; the 1752 K Y metal phase marker does not change the ideal-gas Y(g) function.

P672-Y2O3-c.source_note: Y2O3 formation table, printed p. 475; -455.380 kcal/mol is the elemental-reference 298.15 K cell. The 1330 K alpha-beta transition is printed with 0.310 kcal/mol enthalpy; the post-transition branch is represented by the 1330 K high-phase cell. The table prints a plain 2000 K node with no extrapolation footnote; source limit is 2000 K.

P672-Tl-g.source_note: Printed p. 439, Tl(g) formation table; 43.250 kcal/mol is the elemental 298.15 K anchor for Tl(c,l,g) = Tl(g). Thermal and formation nodes are transcribed from the page image through 2000 K. Printed p. 439 cites Hultgren for the 298.15 K enthalpy and Hilsenrath for the other data; its printed Cp rises from 4.970 cal/mol/K at 900 K to 5.234 at 1746 K, and all printed nodes remain source data. The constant-heat-capacity note for 900-1746 K is printed on p. 438 and belongs to the Tl(c,l,g) metal table. Phase changes at 507 K, 577 K, and boiling at 1746 K are printed on the table.

P672-Tl2O-l.source_note: Printed p. 440, Tl2O(c,l) table. The elemental-reference 298.15 K formation enthalpy is -40.400 kcal/mol for 2Tl(c,l) + 0.5O2(g) = Tl2O(c,l). The page prints an estimated 298 K heat capacity, a 7.210 kcal/mol fusion enthalpy, and liquid nodes at 852, 900, and 1000 K. The 852 K liquid node is selected for the above-melt branch; source limit is 1000 K.

P672-Tl2O-g.source_note: Printed p. 441, Tl2O(g) formation table; 1.500 kcal/mol is the elemental 298.15 K anchor for 2Tl(c,l) + 0.5O2(g) = Tl2O(g). Thermal and formation nodes are transcribed from the page image through 1000 K. The table prints phase changes of elemental Tl at 507 and 577 K.
